source.title: North Down Herald and County Down Independent, 17 January 1920, p. 1: "Bangor Municipal Elections. Results of the Polling" (Castle Electoral Area). First names and initials: Northern Whig, 17 January 1920, p. 6 ("Bangor").
source.publisher: North Down Herald (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: the elected in order, the poll (1,028), spoiled papers (20), quota (127) and the first preferences of the seven elected, as printed; 1,028 less 20 is 1,008 valid votes, and 1,008 / 8 + 1 = 127, the printed quota. The unsuccessful candidates' first preferences (155 between them) and the transfers are not printed
confirmedBy: Bangor register of elections, typed result sheets of the 1920 count pasted in (PRONI LA/20/1/DA/1; Keep note "LA/20/1/DA/1 Part 3", #2 Castle, #0 Dufferin)

note: Proportional representation (single transferable vote) under the Local Government (Ireland) Act 1919; polled 15 January 1920. Results declared 16 January 1920 by the returning officer, James Milliken (town clerk). The area returned 7 members, elected in the order Seyers, Davidson, Gray, M'Kay, Irwin, Campbell, Gibson. Only the first preferences of the elected are printed; Seyers, Davidson, Gray and M'Kay reached the quota on the first count, and the counts at which Irwin, Campbell and Gibson were elected are not reported. The five unsuccessful candidates polled 155 first preferences between them. Gray's 146 is a reading of a blurred figure (possibly 148). No report seen gives party labels.
correctionNote: Every count from the typed result sheet in the register: the elected in order Seyers, Davidson, Gray, M'Kay, Irwin, Campbell, Gibson. Gray had 148 first preferences (previously 146 from a blurred newspaper figure); 148 is the figure with which the first count adds to the 1,008 valid votes. The unsuccessful candidates' first preferences, which the newspaper did not print, are Lightbody 38, M'Conaghie 42, W. M'Murray 36, A. Thomson 24 and Brownfield 13. The non-transferable papers (7 at the sixth count, 15 at the seventh, 29 at the ninth) are approximate readings of the sheet that agree with the totals.
